title: Amputation and ostomy status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM status codes this note supports.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for abdominal status.

HPI: Patient is a 57-year-old woman who previously underwent a surgical ileostomy due to bowel issues. Following that period, she underwent a surgical reversal of the procedure. She reports that since the takedown, she has experienced good bowel function and no significant abdominal discomfort. She presents today for a routine check-up to ensure continued healing and stability of the surgical site. She denies any new pain, changes in stool consistency, or abdominal distention since her last visit.

Medication List:
- Multivitamin daily
- Fiber supplement as needed

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F, BMI 26.4.

Review of Systems:
- Constitutional: Negative
- GI: Positive (Normal bowel movements)
- Musculoskeletal: Negative
- Neurological: Negative
- Integumentary: Negative

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert, and in no acute distress.
Abdomen: Soft, non-distended, and non-tender. Surgical scars from the previous ileostomy and the subsequent reversal are well-healed with no signs of dehiscence or irritation. Bowel sounds are present in all four quadrants.

Assessment:
1. Status post-ileostomy reversal.

Plan:
1. Continue current activity level.
2. Monitor for any signs of abdominal discomfort.
3. Return to clinic in 6 months for routine follow-up.

Electronically signed, 
S. Patel, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: The ileostomy was reversed: the patient no longer has one, so there is no status to report.

distractors.why: A reversed ileostomy is no longer present.
